oldKimi.reason: Historical permission asymmetry disqualifies strict fairness; aggregate-only public evidence not used to invent an arm distribution.

decisions.piAndOpencode: Prior four-pair results and current task-dependent directions do not establish generally unacceptable overhead. Stop treating individual high ratios as a product repair trigger.
decisions.mixedPiB: Two pairs both higher; mean input ratio about 1.408 with low observed native spread. Keep as a focused signal, not dismissed as noise and not enough to establish a universal defect.
decisions.mixedOpencodeA: One higher pair and one near parity; mean input ratio about 1.386. Keep actual spend visible; no consistent direction established from two pairs.
decisions.oldClaude: All four pairs higher, about 1.48 mean input ratio and worse measured quality. Stronger engineering signal, still tied to old source/model/task rather than proof of current defect.
decisions.kimi: Current B both slightly higher but mean input ratio about 1.023; repeated direction alone is not evidence of unacceptable magnitude. A has broad native spread; no guaranteed saving claim.
decisions.next: Do not modify prompts/scheduling or buy further large sweeps to force ratios to 1.0. Prioritize reproducible correctness/accounting failures; cost intervention requires a specific shared mechanism and predetermined material-overhead criterion.

futureComparisonRules: Freeze task commit/materials, success criteria, provider/model/effort, CLI version and memory policy on both sides.
Use independent fresh sessions for repeats while retaining normal history within each long task. Interleave or randomize side order to reduce time-order effects.
Retain pairing/blocking for fair conditions, but judge distributions and aggregate magnitude rather than demanding each pair approach 1.0.
Predeclare sample count or bounded stopping rule and practical margin before new calls. Small n remains inconclusive rather than inviting endless reruns.
A provider switch creates a separate stratum; never switch within an arm or construct a pair from different providers.
